title: Declarative function-descriptor registry and adaptive retry + streaming invocation helpers across SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a small, language-idiomatic helper surface for function/tool calling that: 1) validates user-provided function schemas against a canonical descriptor, 2) normalizes schema metadata across Python/TS/Go SDKs, and 3) exposes ergonomic invocation helpers that handle streaming partials, adaptive retries, and backoff policies. The goal is a consistent developer experience and resilient defaults without sacrificing language ergonomics.
background: We currently have fragmented helper patterns for function/tool invocation across SDKs. Past work introduced strict schema normalizers and runtime validators in isolated PRs, but there is no canonical registry or shared retry/streaming behavior. This causes mismatch between SDKs and increases support burden when customers use function calling at scale or expect deterministic retries for idempotent tool calls.
goals: Define a small canonical function-descriptor format that is serializable across languages and covers name, param schema (JSON Schema-like subset), idempotency hint, invocation timeout, and recommended retry policy.
Implement a lightweight in-SDK registry (declarative) that accepts descriptors and performs validation at registration time and against runtime responses.

Provide invocation helpers that: a) validate payloads pre-send, b) stream partial outputs to callbacks while preserving retry semantics for transient failures, c) perform adaptive backoff respecting per-descriptor policy.
Ship examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go that show sync, async, and streaming usage patterns and document corner cases (schema coercion, unknown fields, large arrays).
Add unit and integration tests that cover cross-language contract behaviors and a small performance/latency benchmark for streaming+retry paths.
tasks: Draft canonical descriptor spec (md) and get PM + security sign-off
Python: implement registry, sync/async invocation helper, streaming adapter, tests
TypeScript: implement same surface with idiomatic Promise/AsyncIterator streaming helpers
Go: implement registry and context-aware invocation helper with explicit cancellation and backoff
Design additions to SDK docs with examples and migration notes
Create integration test matrix: function schema permutations, idempotent vs non-idempotent flags, simulated transient errors
Benchmark streaming latency with/without retries and measure CPU/memory under contention
Open cross-repo PRs and collect reviews from SDK leads and Runtime team
acceptance_criteria: Canonical descriptor spec merged in docs repo and linked from SDK READMEs
Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a Registry API that validates descriptors and rejects incompatible fields at registration time
Invocation helpers handle transient network errors and retry according to descriptor policy; non-idempotent descriptors are not retried by default
Streaming helpers surface partial events to the caller while ensuring that retries restart idempotent invocation from an agreed checkpoint or re-request pattern
End-to-end examples run against staging runtime (manual test) and automated integration tests pass in CI
Telemetry hooks added: per-invocation retry count, total tokens emitted during streaming, and latency histograms
implementation_notes: Key design choices: 1) Keep descriptor JSON small — avoid full JSON Schema; implement a subset we can validate easily in Go/TS/Python. 2) Retry policy must support 'none', 'standard', and 'aggressive' and include max_retries and backoff multiplier. 3) For streaming, adopt a resume token pattern: runtime should emit resume metadata when partial state is safe to replay; SDK helpers will prefer 'resume' over blind retry when available. 4) Expose opt-in telemetry and allow customers to override retry/backoff at call time.
